title: SLA-aware bandwidth fencing and backpressure propagation for scheduled usage shipments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a per-tenant bandwidth-fencing and backpressure propagation layer for scheduled usage exports (CSV/JSONL/S3/webhook delivery). Goal is to prevent noisy tenants from causing cascading delays and timeouts for other customers while preserving SLA commitments (tiered: platinum/gold/silver). This ticket covers design, runtime controls, datastore schema changes for delivery metadata, and the first-pass implementation of per-tenant leaky-bucket rate enforcement on the export orchestration worker pool.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant bandwidth and concurrency quotas configurable via Console and applied by the export orchestrator
Exports for high-priority tenants should maintain 95th-percentile latency target under average cluster load (target defined in release notes)
Backpressure must propagate to scheduler: when a tenant is rate-limited, new export jobs should be delayed and visible in UI with reason and ETA
Exports must be resumable with idempotent manifest checksums and observable retry counts
SLO dashboards and alerts for export queueing latency, rate-limited tenants, and delivery failure rate are present in Grafana
tasks: Design doc: bandwidth fencing model and quota defeinition (done)
Add tenant_quota table to export metadata DB with burst_capacity and sustained_rate (migration + rollback)
Implement leaky-bucket enforcement in export-orchestrator worker (Go) with pluggable token-bucket middleware
Wire Console UI to allow per-customer quota overrides and show current usage/queue position
Integrate backpressure signals into scheduler to pause low-priority jobs and surface ETA
Add manifest checksum + byte-range resume support for S3/HTTP webhook deliveries
Add metrics and alarm rules: export.queue.latency_seconds, export.rate_limited_tenants, export.delivery.failures
E2E test: simulate noisy tenant and verify isolation + priority preservation
Performance test: run canary with production-like dataset and measure P95 latency for platinum tenants
comments: 2026-03-03 - Asha Patel: Initial ticket created after oncall postmortem where a single enterprise tenant saturated the delivery workers causing 2-hour export delays for other customers. Attached design doc link below.

2026-03-05 - Miguel Ortega: Spike prototyped leaky-bucket middleware. Early results show per-worker enforcement reduces observed head-of-line blocking but coordination needed for cross-worker fairness.
2026-03-07 - Review (PM): Thomas Nguyen: Approved prioritization; asked for clear UI text explaining ETA calculations and admin override audit log.

2026-03-09 - Design note: Chose eventual-consistent cross-worker quota tokens via Redis streams with best-effort sync rather than strictly consistent distributed locking to avoid single-point latency amplification. Trade-off: occasional minor quota overshoot allowed during bursts for simplicity and lower tail-latency.
2026-03-11 - QA: Found edge case where webhook backoff combined with rate-limit caused duplicate delivery attempts; fixed by adding idempotency token check and extending manifest TTL.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Ortega: Open PR #4578 implements DB migration and token-bucket middleware. Needs security review for tenant quota controls before deploy to staging. Performance tests scheduled 2026-03-16.
